Why split. The supplied proof (steps 1–8) bundles five separable obligations with narrow interfaces. Four of them are general and reusable.
- isometry_image_integral (step 2): for any isometry Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P and Borel A, Φ(A) is Borel, Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = vol(A), and ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫_A h∘Φ.
- local_plane_tangent (step 4(iii)): a set that coincides with x + V on B(x, δ) has approximate tangent space V at x. This localizes SimonGMT's hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule.
- coord_plane_orientation (step 4(i), plus finrank V_p = k from step 4(iii)): span{e_{ι(j)}} has dimension k and is oriented by ±e_ι, where e_ι(α) = α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(k−1)}).
- face_union_local_plane (steps 1 and 4(ii)): distinct open lattice faces are disjoint, and their union coincides with x + V_p near each of its points. It takes the frozen type of the resolved sibling Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry verbatim as an antecedent (FG), the same way the selected type takes MR.
- finite_piece_imrep (steps 3–6): finitely many disjoint Borel pieces of finite Hᵏ-measure, covered by Lipschitz images, with positive integer multiplicities and k-vectors orienting the approximate tangent planes of their union, form an IMRep. Its action and mass measure are the sums over the pieces.
Unsplit, the Lean proof would be about 450 lines. The node is at depth 5 and the limit is 6, so the children are final leaves. Each child was proved in full against its exact type in scratch (see Verification), so all five are atomic and feasible.

Derivation of the selected statement (the supplied steps 1–8). Intro MR, P, k, s, β, T, hmono, hT, and let FG := Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry, the resolved dependency.
1. Setup.
 - Q₁ := {y : ∀ i, 0 < y_i < 1} is a finite intersection of open coordinate conditions (PiLp.continuous_apply), so it is open and Borel. vol(Q₁) = 1 by FG(0).
 - For p ∈ s, Φ_p(y) := toLp b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} is an isometry, by FG(a) and Isometry.of_dist_eq.
2. Data.
 - For each p with StrictMono p.1, coord_plane_orientation gives finrank V_p = k and e_p with e_p(α) = α(E_p), where e_p and −e_p both orient V_p. Choose these by choice, with junk 0 when p.1 is not StrictMono.
 - Put S := s.filter (β · ≠ 0), F_p := Φ_p(Q₁), m_p := (β p).natAbs, ξ_p := if 0 < β p then e_p else −e_p, and G_p := Φ_p.
3. isometry_image_integral applied to (Φ_p, Q₁): F_p is Borel, Hᵏ(F_p) = 1, and ∫_{F_p} h dHᵏ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy.
4. finite_piece_imrep with U = univ. Its hypotheses hold:
 - F_p is Borel and F_p ⊆ univ, with Hᵏ(F_p) = 1 ≠ ∞.
 - Disjointness is face_union_local_plane (a), applied to S, whose members have StrictMono first components.
 - m_p > 0 (Int.natAbs_pos). G_p is 1-Lipschitz (Isometry.lipschitzWith), and F_p ⊆ range Φ_p.
 - At x = Φ_p(t) ∈ F_p, face_union_local_plane (b) gives δ and the local-plane property of C = ⋃_{q∈S} F_q. local_plane_tangent, with finrank V_p = k, then gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x V_p, and coord_plane_orientation gives IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p V_p.
 The result is R : IMRep univ k with R.action ω = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω) dHᵏ and R.measure univ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p).
5. Representation.
 - T ω = Σ_{p∈s} β_p ∫_{Q₁} ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy = Σ_{p∈S} (same terms) (Finset.sum_filter_of_ne; the dropped terms have β_p = 0).
 - For p ∈ S, combine step 3 with h := ξ_p∘ω, the identity (m_p : ℝ) = |β_p| (Nat.cast_natAbs, Int.cast_abs) and e_p(α) = α(E_p). This gives m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω) dHᵏ = β_p ∫_{Q₁} ω(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy. For β_p < 0, use (−e_p)(α) = −e_p(α) and integral_neg.
 - Hence R.Represents T, so T is integer multiplicity.
6. Mass. MR with U = W = univ gives T.mass = T.massOn univ = R.measure univ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p · 1 = Σ_{p∈S} ofReal|β_p| (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast) = ofReal(Σ_{p∈S}|β_p|) (ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg) = ofReal(Σ_{p∈s}|β_p|) (Finset.sum_filter_of_ne).
7. Dichotomy. If β vanishes on s, then T ω = 0 for every ω, so T = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext, zero_apply). Otherwise |β_p| ≥ 1 for some p ∈ s (Int.one_le_abs), so Σ_q |β_q| ≥ 1 (Finset.single_le_sum) and T.mass ≥ ofReal 1 = 1.
8. k > P needs no special case: then s = ∅.

subproblems.title: Isometric images: Borel, Hᵏ-measure and change of variables
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P be an isometry for the Euclidean metrics, and let A ⊆ Euclid k be a Borel set. Then Φ(A) is Borel, Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Lᵏ(A), and ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy for every function h : Euclid P → ℝ. Here Hᵏ = μHE[k] is Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, Lᵏ = volume is Lebesgue measure on Euclid k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), and the integrals are Bochner integrals (each is 0 when its integrand is not integrable).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (Φ : Euclid k → Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid k)), Isometry Φ → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet (Φ '' A) ∧ μHE[k] (Φ '' A) = volume A ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ x in Φ '' A, h x ∂μHE[k] = ∫ y in A, h (Φ y)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of the selected node dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im (“Change of variables. Φ_p is an isometry, hence a closed embedding and a measurable embedding … F̆_p is Borel; ∫_{F̆_p} h dHᵏ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p y) dy …; Hᵏ(F̆_p) = vol(Q₁) = 1”). It is stated here for an arbitrary isometry Φ and Borel set A; the parent applies it with Φ = Φ_p and A = Q₁. The same type is frozen in the twin branch (root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.…polyhedral_im-a1) under the name cmcdtfrpi_isometry_image_integral. That name is reserved there, so this child is declared under the fresh name Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrpi_isometry_image_integral and proved here.

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k], on Euclid P or on Euclid k as indicated; Lᵏ := volume on Euclid k; μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; Φ_#μ := μ.map Φ.

1. Measurable embedding. Euclid k is complete and Φ is an isometry, so Φ is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding). A closed embedding between Borel spaces is a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding): Φ is injective and measurable, and it maps Borel sets to Borel sets. Hence Φ(A) is Borel (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image). This is the first conclusion.
2. Hᵏ = Lᵏ on Euclid k, by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume k.
3. Measure of the image. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries, for every set: Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = Hᵏ(A) (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). By step 2, Hᵏ(A) = Lᵏ(A). This is the second conclusion.
4. Push-forward identity: Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) = Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A) as measures on Euclid P.
 - For a measurable embedding and every set E, (Φ_#μ)⌞E = Φ_#(μ⌞Φ⁻¹(E)) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map). Apply it with μ := Hᵏ on Euclid k and E := Φ(A).
 - Φ_#Hᵏ = Hᵏ⌞range Φ (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). So the left side is (Hᵏ⌞range Φ)⌞Φ(A) = Hᵏ⌞(Φ(A) ∩ range Φ) (Measure.restrict_restrict; Φ(A) is Borel by step 1), and this is Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) because Φ(A) ⊆ range Φ.
 - On the right side, Φ⁻¹(Φ(A)) = A by injectivity (Set.preimage_image_eq), and Hᵏ⌞A = Lᵏ⌞A by step 2.
5. Change of variables. For a measurable embedding Φ, every measure μ on Euclid k and every function g : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ g d(Φ_#μ) = ∫ g∘Φ dμ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). No measurability or integrability hypothesis is needed: g is AE-strongly measurable for Φ_#μ exactly when g∘Φ is for μ, integrability transfers in the same way, and otherwise both Bochner integrals are 0. Take μ := Lᵏ⌞A and use step 4: ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫ h d(Hᵏ⌞Φ(A)) = ∫ h d(Φ_#(Lᵏ⌞A)) = ∫_A h(Φ(y)) dy. This is the third conclusion.
6. No case distinction is needed. For k = 0, Euclid 0 is a single point and the same lemmas apply verbatim. ∎

Lean note (checked). A proof of exactly this type compiles in the comparator scope (import GMT.Ch07.Submission, the contract's opens, namespace GMT.Ch07), with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only:
 - hemb := hΦ.isClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding, and hemb.measurableSet_image.mpr hA;
 - rw [hΦ.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume k];
 - the identity μHE[k].restrict (Φ '' A) = (volume.restrict A).map Φ, from hemb.restrict_map μHE[k] (Φ '' A) rewritten with hΦ.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Measure.restrict_restrict, Set.inter_eq_left.mpr (Set.image_subset_range _ _), Set.preimage_image_eq _ hemb.injective and the volume identity;
 - finally rw [that identity, hemb.integral_map].
This was re-checked under the declaration name Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfrpi_isometry_image_integral.
proof_key_steps: An isometry from the complete space Euclid k is a closed, hence measurable, embedding, so Φ(A) is Borel.
Hᵏ is isometry-invariant and equals Lebesgue measure on Euclid k, so Hᵏ(Φ(A)) = vol(A).
Hᵏ⌞Φ(A) = Φ_#(vol⌞A), from map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map, injectivity and restrict_restrict.
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives ∫_{Φ(A)} h dHᵏ = ∫_A h∘Φ dy for every h.

subproblems.title: A set that coincides with x + V near x has approximate tangent space V at x
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ Euclid P be an arbitrary set, x ∈ Euclid P, V a linear subspace of Euclid P with finrank V = n, and δ > 0. Suppose that every z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, x) < δ satisfies z ∈ M ⟺ z − x ∈ V. Then V is the approximate tangent space of M at x in the sense of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4, as formalized by SimonGMT's HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V. That is, finrank V = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_V f dHⁿ as r → 0⁺, where η_{x,r}(y) = blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x) and Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (δ : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → 0 < δ → (∀ z : Euclid P, dist z x < δ → (z ∈ M ↔ z - x ∈ V)) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(iii) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im. There, for 0 < r < δ/R, the blow-ups of the carrier agree with V_p on B(0, R), so r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(C)} f dHᵏ is eventually equal to ∫_{V_p} f dHᵏ along 𝓝[>] 0. Here it is stated for an arbitrary set M and subspace V; the local hypothesis is exactly what step 4(ii) provides for the carrier. It generalizes SimonGMT's hasApproximateTangentSpaceAt_submodule (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean), which is the case M = V, x ∈ V.

Notation. η_{x,r}(y) := blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x), and Hⁿ := μHE[n] on Euclid P. By definition, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V means: finrank ℝ V = n, and for every f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) the function r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ tends to ∫_V f dHⁿ along 𝓝[>] 0.

1. finrank ℝ V = n is a hypothesis. Fix f ∈ C_c(Euclid P, ℝ) for the rest of the proof.
2. A ball outside which f vanishes. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄(0, R₀) for some R₀ ∈ ℝ. Put R := max(R₀, 0) + 1. Then R > 0 and R > R₀. If ‖y‖ ≥ R, then y ∉ B̄(0, R₀) ⊇ tsupport f, so f(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence f vanishes outside the open ball B := B(0, R).
3. Localization. For every set S ⊆ Euclid P, measurable or not, ∫_S f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩S} f dHⁿ. Indeed B is open, hence Borel, so (Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B = Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ S) (Measure.restrict_restrict). Since f = 0 off B, ∫ f d((Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
4. Claim: if r > 0 and rR < δ (equivalently 0 < r < δ/R), then B ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B ∩ V.
 (⊆) Let y ∈ B with y = r⁻¹(z − x) for some z ∈ M. Then ‖y‖ = r⁻¹‖z − x‖ < R, so ‖z − x‖ < rR < δ, i.e. dist(z, x) < δ. By the hypothesis, z ∈ M gives z − x ∈ V. Since V is a subspace, y = r⁻¹(z − x) ∈ V.
 (⊇) Let y ∈ B ∩ V and put z := x + r y. Then z − x = r y ∈ V, and dist(z, x) = ‖r y‖ = r‖y‖ < rR < δ, so z ∈ M by the hypothesis. Also η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(r y) = y because r ≠ 0. So y ∈ η_{x,r}(M).
5. For every r with 0 < r < δ/R, steps 3, 4 and 3 again give
 ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B∩V} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ.
6. Since δ/R > 0, the interval (0, δ/R) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). By step 5, r ↦ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ is eventually equal along 𝓝[>] 0 to the constant ∫_V f dHⁿ, so it tends to that constant (Filter.tendsto_congr' with tendsto_const_nhds). Since f was arbitrary, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x V holds. ∎ No measurability of M is used, and the case n = 0, V = {0} needs no special treatment.

Lean note (checked). A proof of exactly this type, following steps 1–6, compiles in the comparator scope with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
 - blowUpMap lives in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03, which the contract does not open, so write Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap. It satisfies blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹ • (y − x) by rfl: unfold it, then use norm_smul, abs_inv, abs_of_pos and inv_mul_lt_iff₀.
 - R₀ comes from f.hasCompactSupport.isBounded.subset_closedBall 0.
 - Localization: rw [← Measure.restrict_restrict Metric.isOpen_ball.measurableSet, setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero hfz].
 - Limit: (Filter.tendsto_congr' _).2 tendsto_const_nhds, with filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsGT _].
proof_key_steps: tsupport f is compact, so f = 0 outside B(0, R) for some R > 0.
For 0 < r < δ/R, B(0,R) ∩ η_{x,r}(M) = B(0,R) ∩ V: |z − x| = r|η_{x,r}(z)| < δ, then apply the local hypothesis in both directions.
Restricting to the Borel ball does not change ∫ f, so ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ for all small r > 0.
The function is eventually constant along 𝓝[>] 0, which gives the limit; finrank V = n is a hypothesis.

subproblems.title: Coordinate k-planes: dimension k and unit orientations ±e_ι
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let ι : Fin k → Fin P be strictly increasing. Put τ_j := e_{ι(j)} = EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 (standard basis vectors of Euclid P) and V := span{τ_j : j ∈ Fin k}. Then finrank V = k. Moreover, there is a k-vector e ∈ MultiVector P k (a continuous linear functional on k-covectors) with e(α) = α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for every k-covector α, such that both e and −e are unit orientations of V (IsUnitOrientationOf).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (ι : Fin k → Fin P), StrictMono ι → Module.finrank ℝ (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P))) = k ∧ ∃ e : MultiVector P k, (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, e α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf e (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P))) ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (-e) (Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(i) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im (“τ := E_p is orthonormal (EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single composed with the injective ι), span(range τ) = V_p, and ξ(x)(α) = sign(β_p)·α(τ) for all α, with sign(β_p) ∈ {1, −1}”). It also covers “finrank V_p = k (finrank_span_eq_card; E_p is linearly independent)” from step 4(iii), and the k-vector e_p := (α ↦ α(E_p)) of the Notation paragraph.

Notation. τ_j := EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) 1 for j ∈ Fin k, and V := span_ℝ(range τ).

1. τ is orthonormal. The standard basis i ↦ EuclideanSpace.single i 1 of Euclid P is orthonormal: it is the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), or equivalently use EuclideanSpace.orthonormal_single. Since ι is strictly increasing, it is injective, so τ = (standard basis) ∘ ι is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp).
2. finrank V = k. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent). So finrank_ℝ span(range τ) = card(Fin k) = k (finrank_span_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin).
3. The k-vector e.
 - Let ev(α) := α(τ_0, …, τ_{k−1}) for α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) k, the continuous alternating k-linear maps Euclid P → ℝ.
 - ev is linear: addition and scalar multiplication of alternating maps are pointwise, so ev(α + β) = ev(α) + ev(β) and ev(cα) = c·ev(α) hold by definition.
 - ev is bounded: |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ ∏_j ‖τ_j‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and ‖τ_j‖ = 1 because τ_j is a standard basis vector. So |ev(α)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
 Hence e := LinearMap.mkContinuous ev 1 is a continuous linear functional, i.e. e ∈ MultiVector P k, and e(α) = α(τ) for every α. This is the first property of e.
4. IsUnitOrientationOf e V. Take τ as the witness. It is orthonormal (step 1), span(range τ) = V by definition, and e(α) = α(τ) for all α. This is the first alternative of the definition.
5. IsUnitOrientationOf (−e) V. Take the same witness τ. Negation of continuous linear maps is pointwise, so (−e)(α) = −e(α) = −α(τ) for all α. This is the second alternative. ∎ For k = 0, τ is the empty family, V = {0}, finrank V = 0, and e evaluates a 0-covector at the empty tuple; every step holds verbatim.

Lean note (checked). A proof of exactly this type compiles in the comparator scope with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
 - Orthonormality: convert (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).orthonormal.comp ι hι.injective using 1, then funext and simp [EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply].
 - finrank: rw [finrank_span_eq_card horth.linearIndependent, Fintype.card_fin].
 - e: the linear map {toFun := fun α => α τ, map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl, map_smul' := fun _ _ => rfl}, made continuous by LinearMap.mkContinuous with constant 1. The bound comes from α.le_opNorm τ and ∏ j, ‖τ j‖ = 1 (simp).
 - Both orientations hold with witness τ and the equalities by rfl; (−e) α = −(e α) is rfl.
proof_key_steps: τ = (standard basis) ∘ ι is orthonormal because ι is injective.
finrank span(range τ) = k by linear independence of an orthonormal family.
Evaluation α ↦ α(τ) is linear and bounded by ‖α‖, which gives e ∈ MultiVector P k with e(α) = α(τ).
τ witnesses IsUnitOrientationOf for e (sign +) and for −e (sign −).

subproblems.title: Open lattice faces are disjoint, and their union is flat near each of its points
subproblems.statement: Assume (FG), the exact frozen Lean type of Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry: for all P, k, the open unit cube has volume 1, and for index pairs p, q with strictly increasing first components the face maps are isometries, have diameter ≤ √P on the closed cube, and an open face point Φ_p(y) is at distance ≥ 1 or ≥ min(y_j, 1 − y_j) (some j) from any point Φ_q(y') of a different closed face. Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let S be a finite set of pairs p = (ι, b), with b ∈ ℤ^P and ι : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing for every p ∈ S. Write Φ_p(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid k, Q₁ := (0,1)^k, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span{e_{ι(j)} : j ∈ Fin k}. Then (a) F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅ for distinct p, q ∈ S; and (b) for every p ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁ there is δ > 0 such that every z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, Φ_p(t)) < δ satisfies z ∈ C ⟺ z − Φ_p(t) ∈ V_p.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P k : ℕ), volume {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} = 1 ∧ ∀ p q : (Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ), StrictMono p.1 → StrictMono q.1 → (∀ y y' : Euclid k, dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = dist y y') ∧ (∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ≤ Real.sqrt P) ∧ (p ≠ q → ∀ y y' : Euclid k, (∀ j, 0 < y j ∧ y j < 1) → (∀ i, 0 ≤ y' i ∧ y' i ≤ 1) → 1 ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∨ ∃ j, min (y j) (1 - y j) ≤ dist (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y' j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)))) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (S : Finset ((Fin k → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))), (∀ p ∈ S, StrictMono p.1) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, p ≠ q → Disjoint ((fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}) ((fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1})) ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ t : Euclid k, (∀ i, 0 < t i ∧ t i < 1) → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ z : Euclid P, dist z (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, t j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) < δ → (z ∈ ⋃ q ∈ S, (fun y : Euclid k => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) '' {y : Euclid k | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1} ↔ z - (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, t j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (range (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ) : Fin k → Euclid P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4(ii) of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im: the open faces F̆_p are pairwise disjoint, and C ∩ B(x, δ) = Π_p ∩ B(x, δ). The isometry and separation facts come from the antecedent (FG). (FG) is verbatim the frozen type of Submission.dimred_mbl_dtfr_face_geometry, the selected node's resolved sibling dependency; the parent discharges (FG) with that declaration.

Notation. For p = (ι, b): Φ_p(y) := WithLp.toLp 2 b + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ Euclid k, with e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Also Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}, F̆_p := Φ_p(Q₁), C := ⋃_{q∈S} F̆_q and V_p := span_ℝ{e_{ι(j)} : j ∈ Fin k}. Every p ∈ S has a strictly increasing first component.

0. Facts from (FG), applied at (P, k). For pairs p, q whose first components are strictly increasing:
 (iso) dist(Φ_p y, Φ_p y') = dist(y, y') for all y, y' ∈ Euclid k;
 (sep) if p ≠ q, y ∈ Q₁ and y' ∈ [0,1]^k, then 1 ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y'), or min(y_j, 1 − y_j) ≤ dist(Φ_p y, Φ_q y') for some j.
1. Part (a), disjointness. Let p ≠ q in S, and suppose w ∈ F̆_p ∩ F̆_q, say w = Φ_p(t) = Φ_q(t') with t, t' ∈ Q₁. Since Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k, (sep) applies to (p, q, t, t'). But dist(Φ_p t, Φ_q t') = dist(w, w) = 0. The first alternative gives 1 ≤ 0, which is false. The second gives min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 0 for some j, which is false because 0 < t_j < 1. So F̆_p ∩ F̆_q = ∅.
2. Part (b), choice of δ. Fix p = (ι, b) ∈ S and t ∈ Q₁, and let x := Φ_p(t). Let D be the finite set {1} ∪ {min(t_j, 1 − t_j) : j ∈ Fin k}; it is nonempty because it contains 1. Put δ := min D. Every element of D is positive, so δ > 0. Also δ ≤ 1, and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j. (For k = 0, D = {1} and δ = 1.)
 Now let z ∈ Euclid P with dist(z, x) < δ. We show z ∈ C ⟺ z − x ∈ V_p.
3. (⇒) Suppose z ∈ C, so z = Φ_q(t') for some q ∈ S and t' ∈ Q₁.
 - If q ≠ p, apply (sep) to (p, q, t, t'); this is allowed since t' ∈ Q₁ ⊆ [0,1]^k. It gives 1 ≤ dist(x, z), or min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ dist(x, z) for some j. But dist(x, z) = dist(z, x) < δ, with δ ≤ 1 and δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j). So both alternatives are impossible.
 - Hence q = p. Then z − x = Φ_p(t') − Φ_p(t) = Σ_j (t'_j − t_j) e_{ι(j)}, because the constant toLp(b) cancels. This is a linear combination of the e_{ι(j)}, so z − x ∈ V_p (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, with coefficients t'_j − t_j).
4. (⇐) Suppose z − x ∈ V_p.
 - V_p is spanned by the finite family (e_{ι(j)})_{j ∈ Fin k}, so there is c : Fin k → ℝ with Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = z − x (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun).
 - Let t' := t + toLp(c) ∈ Euclid k, so t'_j = t_j + c_j. Then Φ_p(t') = toLp(b) + Σ_j t_j e_{ι(j)} + Σ_j c_j e_{ι(j)} = x + (z − x) = z.
 - By (iso), dist(t', t) = dist(Φ_p t', Φ_p t) = dist(z, x) < δ. A coordinate distance is at most the Euclidean distance (PiLp.dist_apply_le), so |c_j| = |t'_j − t_j| ≤ dist(t', t) < δ ≤ min(t_j, 1 − t_j) for each j.
 - Hence t'_j = t_j + c_j > t_j − min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≥ 0, and t'_j < t_j + min(t_j, 1 − t_j) ≤ 1. So t' ∈ Q₁ and z = Φ_p(t') ∈ F̆_p. Since p ∈ S, z ∈ C.
5. Steps 3 and 4 prove the equivalence for every z with dist(z, x) < δ. This completes part (b). ∎

Lean note (checked). A proof of exactly this type compiles in the comparator scope with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
 - Start with intro FG P k S hS and obtain ⟨-, FGpq⟩ := FG P k.
 - Image-membership hypotheses arrive beta-unreduced, e.g. (fun y => …) t' = (fun y => …) t; use beta_reduce at them before rewriting.
 - δ := (insert 1 (Finset.univ.image fun j => min (t j) (1 - t j))).min' (Finset.insert_nonempty _ _), with Finset.lt_min'_iff and Finset.min'_le.
 - In (⇒), close the q = p case with Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun, sub_smul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib and abel.
 - In (⇐), set t' := t + WithLp.toLp 2 c. Coordinates: t' j = t j + c j by PiLp.add_apply and PiLp.toLp_apply. Then |c j| < δ from PiLp.dist_apply_le t' t j, and finish with abs_lt and linarith.
proof_key_steps: From (FG): each face map is an isometry, and an open face is separated from every other closed face (distance ≥ 1 or ≥ min(t_j, 1 − t_j)).
Disjointness: a common point would have distance 0 from itself, which contradicts separation.
⇒: a nearby point of another face contradicts separation, so z lies on the same face and z − x = Σ (t'_j − t_j) e_{ι(j)} ∈ V_p.
⇐: write z − x = Σ c_j e_{ι(j)}. By the isometry, |c_j| ≤ |z − x| < δ, so t + c ∈ (0,1)^k and z = Φ_p(t + c) ∈ C.

subproblems.title: A finite disjoint family of oriented rectifiable pieces gives an IMRep with additive action and mass
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, I a type, U ⊆ Euclid P, and S ⊆ I finite. For each p ∈ S let F_p ⊆ Euclid P be Borel with F_p ⊆ U and Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞, let m_p ∈ ℕ be positive, ξ_p ∈ MultiVector P k a k-vector, and G_p : Euclid k → Euclid P a Lipschitz map with F_p ⊆ range G_p. Suppose the F_p (p ∈ S) are pairwise disjoint, and at every x ∈ F_p some subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q, where C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q. Then there is an IMRep R in U of dimension k such that R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and R.measure(Euclid P) = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p). Here Hᵏ = μHE[k].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (I : Type) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : Finset I) (F : I → Set (Euclid P)) (m : I → ℕ) (ξ : I → MultiVector P k) (G : I → Euclid k → Euclid P), (∀ p ∈ S, MeasurableSet (F p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ U) → (∀ p ∈ S, μHE[k] (F p) ≠ ∞) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, p ≠ q → Disjoint (F p) (F q)) → (∀ p ∈ S, 0 < m p) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, F p ⊆ range (G p)) → (∀ p ∈ S, ∀ x ∈ F p, ∃ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (⋃ q ∈ S, F q) x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ p) Q) → ∃ R : IMRep U k, (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ) * ∫ x in F p, ξ p ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μHE[k]) ∧ R.measure univ = ∑ p ∈ S, (m p : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[k] (F p)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–6 of the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dtfr_polyhedral_im: the triple (C, θ, ξ), its IMRep fields, the splitting of the action integral over the disjoint pieces, and the computation of R.measure. Here they are stated for an arbitrary finite family of disjoint pieces. The parent instantiates it with the open faces F̆_p = Φ_p((0,1)^k), m_p = |β_p|, ξ_p = sign(β_p) e_p and G_p = Φ_p. The contract's IMRep encodes Simon, Ch. 6, Definition 3.1, and IMRep.action encodes 6.3.1 (‡).

Notation. Hᵏ := μHE[k] on Euclid P, and C := ⋃_{q∈S} F_q.

1. Carrier. C is Borel, as a finite union of Borel sets (Finset.measurableSet_biUnion). C ⊆ U because each F_q ⊆ U.
2. Uniqueness of the piece. If p, q ∈ S, q ≠ p and x ∈ F_p, then x ∉ F_q, by the disjointness hypothesis.
3. Multiplicity. Let θ(x) := Σ_{q∈S} 1_{F_q}(x) · m_q ∈ ℕ, the sum of the indicators of the F_q with constant values m_q.
 - θ is measurable: each summand is the indicator of a Borel set with a constant value, and a finite sum of measurable ℕ-valued functions is measurable (Finset.measurable_sum).
 - θ(x) = m_p for x ∈ F_p with p ∈ S: by step 2 every other summand vanishes (Finset.sum_eq_single).
 - Hence θ > 0 on C, since every point of C lies in some F_p with m_p > 0.
4. Orientation. List S as p₁, …, p_N (S.toList). Define ξ(x) := ξ_{p_i} for the least i with x ∈ F_{p_i}, and ξ(x) := 0 if x ∉ C. Formally, ξ(x) is the right fold over the list of (q, acc) ↦ (if x ∈ F_q then ξ_q else acc), starting from 0.
 - By induction on the list, ξ is strongly measurable: the empty fold is constant, and each step is an if-then-else on a Borel set between a constant and a strongly measurable function (StronglyMeasurable.ite). So ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞C.
 - ξ(x) = ξ_p whenever x ∈ F_p and p ∈ S, by step 2 and induction on the list: every entry q ≠ p has x ∉ F_q, and the entry p returns ξ_p.
 By disjointness this ξ is the same function as the supplied proof's Σ_{q∈S} 1_{F_q} ξ_q; the fold only changes how it is written. In Lean the sum route through Finset.stronglyMeasurable_sum needs ContinuousAdd (MultiVector P k), and that instance does not synthesize in the frozen environment (checked).
5. Countable rectifiability.
 - With the list p₁, …, p_N, define F_j := G_{p_{j+1}} for j < N, and F_j := the constant map 0 for j ≥ N. Each F_j is Lipschitz, by hypothesis or because it is constant.
 - Every x ∈ C lies in some F_p ⊆ range G_p, and p = p_{j+1} for some j < N. So C ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with M₀ := ∅, and Hᵏ(∅) = 0.
 This is CountablyRectifiable k C. (Equivalently: countablyRectifiable_range for each G_p, then countablyRectifiable_iUnion and CountablyRectifiable.mono, as in the supplied proof.)
6. Total weight. The F_p (p ∈ S) are pairwise disjoint and Borel, so ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ (lintegral_biUnion_finset). On F_p, θ = m_p by step 3, so ∫⁻_{F_p} θ dHᵏ = m_p Hᵏ(F_p) (setLIntegral_congr_fun, lintegral_const, Measure.restrict_apply_univ). Hence ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), which is finite because every Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞ (ENNReal.sum_ne_top, ENNReal.mul_ne_top).
7. Local integrability. For every compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ < ∞ (lintegral_mono_set).
8. Orients. Let x ∈ C, so x ∈ F_p for some p ∈ S. The hypothesis gives Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k C x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_p Q, and ξ(x) = ξ_p by step 4. So the orients condition holds at every point of C. Since C is Borel, it holds Hᵏ⌞C-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem).
9. Steps 1 and 3–8 verify every field of IMRep U k for R := (C, θ, ξ).
10. Action. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U), and write ω also for the underlying form. It is C^∞, hence continuous, with compact support. By definition, R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x) · ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x).
 - For p ∈ S let g_p(x) := m_p · ξ_p(ω(x)). g_p is continuous, since ξ_p is a continuous linear functional. Its support lies in the support of ω, because ξ_p(0) = 0, so g_p has compact support.
 - Hᵏ⌞F_p is a finite measure, hence finite on compact sets, so g_p is integrable for it (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
 - On F_p the integrand θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) equals g_p(x), by steps 3 and 4. Since F_p is Borel, the integrand is integrable on F_p (IntegrableOn.congr_fun).
 - The Bochner integral is additive over finitely many pairwise disjoint Borel sets (integral_biUnion_finset). So R.action(ω) = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} ∫_{F_p} m_p ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω(x)) dHᵏ(x) (setIntegral_congr_fun, integral_const_mul).
11. Mass measure. R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞C).withDensity θ. So R.measure(Euclid P) = ∫⁻ θ d(Hᵏ⌞C) = ∫⁻_C θ dHᵏ = Σ_{p∈S} m_p Hᵏ(F_p), by withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_univ and step 6. ∎ If S = ∅, then C = ∅, θ = 0 and ξ = 0: every field holds trivially, and both identities read 0 = 0.

Lean note (checked). A proof of exactly this type (about 150 lines, following steps 1–11) compiles in the comparator scope with axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound only.
 - Use classical. Take θ := fun x => ∑ q ∈ S, (F q).indicator (fun _ => m q) x, with Finset.measurable_sum S (fun q hq => measurable_const.indicator (hFm q hq)).
 - Take ξf := fun x => S.toList.foldr (fun q acc => if x ∈ F q then ξ q else acc) 0. Prove a list-induction lemma for StronglyMeasurable.ite (hl a List.mem_cons_self) stronglyMeasurable_const ih, and one for the value ξ p.
 - Rectifiability witness: ⟨∅, measure_empty, fun j => if h : j < L.length then G (L.get ⟨j, h⟩) else fun _ => 0, _, _⟩, using List.get_mem, List.mem_iff_get and Finset.mem_toList.
 - Build R with the structure literal { carrier := C, mult := θ, orient := ξf, … }. The two goals then follow by show/defeq: show ∫ x in C, ((θ x : ℕ) : ℝ) * ξf x (ω x) ∂μHE[k] = _ and show ((μHE[k].restrict C).withDensity _) univ = _.
 - Integrability on F p: provide the instance IsFiniteMeasure ((μHE[k]).restrict (F p)) via Measure.restrict_apply_univ, then use Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport with hωcs.mono, where ω.2.1.1.continuous and ω.2.1.2 give continuity and compact support of ω.
proof_key_steps: Carrier C = ⋃ F_p is Borel and contained in U. It is countably k-rectifiable via the Lipschitz maps G_p, padded with constant maps and M₀ = ∅.
θ = Σ m_q 1_{F_q} and ξ = ξ_p on F_p (list fold of if-then-else). By disjointness θ = m_p > 0 and ξ = ξ_p on F_p; both are (strongly) measurable.
The orients condition holds at every point of C by hypothesis, hence a.e. on the Borel set C.
The lintegral splits over the disjoint pieces: ∫⁻_C θ = Σ m_p Hᵏ(F_p) < ∞, which gives local integrability and R.measure(Euclid P).
The action splits the same way: action = Σ m_p ∫_{F_p} ξ_p(ω), since each integrand is continuous with compact support on a finite-measure piece.
